items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: "My job with the Duke Ellington band... My job was to hold at that level"

ctx.x: Yeah, come to New York. Duke say

"You know what you're doing." I say, 'Man, New York's my town, don't worry about it. New York's my town." I knew Willie "the Lion" and Lucky and all them guys, and in the meantime I used to go there and rehearse every Sunday. I belonged to the Clef Club. That was big, that was big like the union is now. We had all the big jobs. / Wanamaker and all them people, had all them jobs. I was the youngest member in the Clef Club. items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: We set in with the symphony orchestra... That's the first time Duke played it... Duke and I regretted... nobody put it on tape or record. That was the greatest thing we ever played.

ctx.x: leads me right-- I remember--my memory of this symphony orchestra played all of our tunes. We set in with the symphony orchestra. We were right in the middle of the symphony orchestra, 100 or so of us. And we played -- I don't know, I'm quite sure we played "Black, Brown and Beige." That's the first time Duke played it. Because the symphony orchestra was so enthused about this particular number, "Black, Brown and Beige." Of course, they played a lot of our different tunes, you know. And we had a field day, man.…

And the only thing Duke and I regretted, Duke and the boys regretted rather, nobody put it on tape or record. That was the greatest thing we ever played. The greatest. That was the greatest concert or the greatest thing we ever done. Everyone said it. And we had guys, because we recorded all the time. How they missed that, I'll never know. How they ever missed that I will never, never know.
